newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks hold the line at open.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks hold the line at open.

text.p: The Australian share market held the line at the opening on Thursday, modest bargain hunting in the resource leaders ensuring a steady start after two consecutive down days.
At the opening, the All Ordinaries index reamined steady with Wednesday's close at 2235.1. September share price index futures also steadied at 2234, a 1.1 point discount to the underlying index.
Brokers said a rebound in commodity prices had seen the miners, and BHP in particular, bounce back from what had been a possibly oversold position.

"BHP is doing a little better. It (selling) may have been overdone in the last two days," said dealer Hamish Dee of Brisbane-based brokerage Lance Jones, adding that stronger commodity prices had assisted the morning's modest rebound.
"A bounce in commodity prices overnight has been a good thing there."
Among the industrials, Dee noted National Australia Bank's firm showing in an otherwise lacklustre bank group.
"It has had some positive press of late and Merrill Lynch has picked it as its favoured Australian bank," Dee said.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about eight to seven, while about 47 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
